document.title: Deputy Secretary Armitage's Meeting with Pakistan Intel Chief Mahmud: You're Either With Us or You're Not (State 157813) [Version 1]
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret] Armitage meets ISI Chief Mahmoud Ahmed the day after 9/11 and presents a 'stark choice': Pakistan must stand with the U.S. or against it, with 'no grey.' Mahmud pledges 'unqualified support' and denies Pakistan was ever 'in bed' with those threatening U.S. interests, which conflicts with U.S. intelligence on Pakistani support for the Taliban. Version 1 contains more released text.

events.description: Terrorist attacks in New York and Washington.
Armitage meets ISI chief Mahmud for 15 minutes; says Pakistan is either with US or not; Mahmud pledges unqualified support.
Armitage met ISI chief Mahmud Ahmed for 15 minutes and delivered the 'with us or not' message.
President Bush's address to the nation referring to those who harbor terrorists.
Musharraf extended an offer of cooperation through Mahmud.
Terrorist attacks on New York and Washington; info pointed toward al-Qa'ida.
President Bush addressed the nation vowing to go after those who harbored terrorists.
Armitage met ISI chief Mahmud at 11:00 AM for 15 minutes, delivering the 'with us or not' message.

relationships.detail: Armitage delivered stark choice message to the ISI director.
relationships.quote: DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE MET PAKISTANI INTER-SERVICES INTELLIGENCE DIRECTORATE (ISI-D) DIRECTOR MAHMUD AHMED ON SEPTEMBER 12

relationships.detail: Mahmud acted on Musharraf's instructions and promised to report back.
relationships.quote: HE HAD BEEN INSTRUCTED BY PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF TO STAY IN WASHINGTON

relationships.detail: Mahmud is ISI-D Director.
relationships.quote: INTER-SERVICES INTELLIGENCE DIRECTORATE (ISI-D) DIRECTOR MAHMUD AHMED

relationships.detail: Armitage asked the ambassador to deliver his message to Musharraf.
relationships.quote: HE WOULD ASK AMBASSADOR CHAMBERLIN TO DELIVER TO PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF

relationships.detail: Al-Qa'ida in Afghanistan; Bush referred to those harboring terrorists, thinking of the Taliban.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT BUSH HAD THE TALIBAN VERY MUCH IN MIND WHEN HE TOLD THE NATION

relationships.detail: Armitage met ISI Director Mahmud on September 12 for 15 minutes to deliver a stern message on Pakistan's role after 9/11.
relationships.quote: DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE MET PAKISTANI INTER-SERVICES INTELLIGENCE DIRECTORATE (ISI-D) DIRECTOR MAHMUD AHMED ON SEPTEMBER 12 FOR 15 MINUTES

relationships.detail: Mahmud Ahmed is identified as the ISI Directorate Director.
relationships.quote: INTER-SERVICES INTELLIGENCE DIRECTORATE (ISI-D) DIRECTOR MAHMUD AHMED

relationships.detail: Mahmud was instructed by President Musharraf to stay in Washington and offer Pakistan's unqualified support.
relationships.quote: HE HAD BEEN INSTRUCTED BY PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF TO STAY IN WASHINGTON AND OFFER PAKISTAN'S "UNQUALIFIED SUPPORT

relationships.detail: Armitage asked Ambassador Chamberlin to deliver his message to President Musharraf as soon as possible.
relationships.quote: ONE WHICH HE WOULD ASK AMBASSADOR CHAMBERLIN TO DELIVER TO PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF JUST AS SOON AS POSSIBLE

relationships.detail: Ambassador was to deliver Armitage's message to Musharraf at the earliest opportunity (requested action).
relationships.quote: AMBASSADOR SHOULD SEEK EARLIEST OPPORTUNITY To REINFORCE DEPUTY SECRETARY'S MESSAGE TO PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF

relationships.detail: Mahmud claimed to represent his President and pledged Pakistan's unqualified support.
relationships.quote: MAHMUD; CLAIMING TO BE REPRESENTING HIS PRESIDENT IN THIS MATTER, ASSURED ARMITAGE THAT HE COULD COUNT ON PAKISTAN'S "UNQUALIFIED SUPPORT,"

relationships.detail: Musharraf is President of Pakistan.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF'S INSTRUCTIONS

relationships.detail: Armitage is Deputy Secretary of State.
relationships.quote: DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE MET PAKISTANI INTER-SERVICES INTELLIGENCE

relationships.detail: Al-Qa'ida and bin Ladin are expected to be named as culprits in the investigation.
relationships.quote: QUITE PROBABLE THAT AL QAIDA AND USAMA BIN LADEN WOULD BE FINGERED AS OUR INVESTIGATION CONTINUES

relationships.detail: Armitage noted perception that some in Pakistani society were sympathetic with the Taliban; Bush's 'harboring' remark was aimed at the Taliban.
relationships.quote: SOME IN PAKISTANI SOCIETY WERE VERY SYMPATHETIC WITH THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Bush's reference to those harboring terrorists specifically meant the Taliban.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT BUSH, IN SPEAKING OF THOSE WHO HARBORED TERRORISTS IN HIS ADDRESS TO THE NATION LAST NIGHT, WAS SPECIFICALLY THINKING OF THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Implied: Taliban are those harboring terrorists (al-Qa'ida).
relationships.quote: THOSE WHO HARBORED TERRORISTS

relationships.detail: Cable from Powell reports the meeting; Mahmud promised to report to his own president.
relationships.quote: MAHMUD CONCLUDED BY PROMISING TO REPORT THIS CONVERSATION PROMPTLY TO HIS PRESIDENT

relationships.detail: Armitage recalled that when Pakistan lost its president, he lost a friend (referring to Zia).
relationships.quote: WHEN PAKISTAN LOST ITS PRESIDENT, HE HAD LOST A FRIEND, AS WELL AS OUR AMERICAN AMBASSADOR AND GENERAL WASSOM

relationships.detail: Mahmud claimed to represent his president and conveyed Musharraf's offer of cooperation.
relationships.quote: OFFER OF COOPERATION THAT PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF HAD EXTENDED THROUGH GENERAL MAHMUD THIS MORNING

key_claims: US information on 12 Sept 2001 pointed strongly to bin Ladin's al-Qa'ida in Afghanistan.
Armitage told ISI chief Mahmud that Pakistan was either with the US or against it, with no grey area.
Mahmud pledged Pakistan's 'unqualified support' on Musharraf's instructions.
The US signaled possible lifting of sanctions on Pakistan as an incentive.
Armitage noted a perception that some in Pakistani society were sympathetic to the Taliban and that Bush meant the Taliban when speaking of harborers.
